description: Interactive graph construction tool for Grade 7 Mathematics — Building Double Bar Graphs. Redesigned with Singularity Design System. Two problem tabs: Superpower Survey and Jodhpur Temperature. Each has a blank graph canvas with gridlines, X-axis category labels, and Y-axis. Student first picks a scale from radio buttons, then constructs bars by dragging or typing values. Correct bars lock with green checkmarks. A final Insights panel highlights key observations.
subject: Mathematics
topic: Superpower Survey and Temperature Double Bar Graph
learningObjectives: Tally raw survey responses into frequency counts
Select an appropriate scale for a bar graph given the data range
Construct a double bar graph with correct bar heights for two groups
Compare and interpret data across categories and groups
Identify patterns and draw insights from visualised data

teachingNotes.superpowerSurvey: First have the student look at the raw letter codes and tally them (connects to data organisation). Then discuss scale choice: if max value is 13, a scale of 2 or 3 works well. After building, ask: 'What story does the graph tell? Which power is most popular in Grade 5 vs Grade 9?'
teachingNotes.jodhpurTemperature: For the temperature data, discuss why the scale matters: if the max is 43°C, a scale of 4 or 5 keeps the graph manageable. After building, ask: 'Can you guess which two months these days might belong to?' Day 1 looks like December/January, Day 2 like May/June.
teachingNotes.general: After both graphs are built, ask: 'What story does each graph tell? In the superpower survey, which power is most popular in Grade 5 vs Grade 9? For temperatures, how does the pattern change between morning and afternoon?'

instructionsForStudent: Choose a data set and build your own double bar graph! First, select an appropriate scale from the options. Then, for each category, set the bar heights for both groups. The tool will check if your bars match the data. Can you build a graph that clearly shows the comparison?
